Hi all — attaching the artifacts Rafael suggested and adding a short narrative below. I stored the files in a secure Drive link (see related_links) and attached PDFs here for quick review.

Attachments included:
- redwood-kms-architecture.pdf (diagram; shows logical separation between customer KEKs in Dedicated via HSM, our managed KMS for Hosted, and network boundaries)
- key-rotation-policy-v2.docx (policy; rotation schedule: KEK annually, DEK rolling rotation every 90 days; emergency rotation procedure included)
- soc2-crypto-controls-extract.pdf (SOC 2 excerpt describing encryption controls and attestations)

Short narrative for SIG/CAIQ:
- Encryption at rest: All customer data is encrypted with application-level DEKs that are themselves encrypted under KEKs stored in KMS. For Dedicated we surface an HSM-backed KEK (nCipher/Thales) in the customer VPC; for Hosted we manage KEKs in a hardened KMS cluster with HSM-backed root keys. Full-disk encryption is enabled on worker volumes with LUKS; S3 buckets use server-side encryption with customer keys where requested.
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers (ECDHE + AES-GCM); mTLS used between internal services where applicable. We maintain a minimum cipher suite baseline and rotate certs via our cert-manager pipeline.
- Key rotation: KEKs: annual rotation with key wrapping and staged rollover; DEKs: automated rotation on a 90-day cadence or on-demand via API. Rotation failures trigger PagerDuty alerts and an audit ticket.
- Audit/logs: KMS calls are logged to a dedicated audit cluster (immutable retention 2 years for SOC2 customers). We can provide summarized logs for audit (timestamp, operation type, key id) with request-specific redaction. Raw logs contain tokenized identifiers and are not shareable outside legal controls.

Let me know if AlphaSys needs vendor attestation documents for our HSM provider — we can surface the FIPS/HSM cert pages.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
